submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad head: most ordinary prose and code crosses the active line weakly (about 0.8-1.7, often on a verb, preposition or 'and' shortly after the opener; 9 of 10 varied plain sentences and 7 of 20 'The N V ...' sentences crossed), so predict ordinary text active-weak. It is strong (above about 2.0) on the token one to four positions after a structural anchor that it attends to almost entirely: the day number and comma after a month name ('November 3,'), ' from' and the quote after 'import X', the '{' after '\frac', ';'/' without' after 'WARRANTY', '=' after 'Suppose 2*z'; predicted inactive (below 0.25 x max) is a whole text that is only a comma-and-space separated list of 5-8 plain integers 0-99 (9-15 tokens, no other words, e.g. '37, 2, 53, 71, 82, 12').
